messages:
jordan: Heads-up — ran into a nasty perf cliff with paged KV + attention kernel when pages get heavily fragmented. Repro on long-chat workloads (>8k tokens).

sara: ah — what cliff? latency spike? memory errors?

jordan: tail latency spikes ~3-4x at 95/99p. root cause: kernel expects contiguous KV blocks for multi-head gather; when pages are fragmented we do either memcopy into a temp slab or fallback to CPU kernel. memcopy is expensive for large KV sizes.

kevin: can you paste the failing stack/log?

jordan: snippet and perf notes below:
```
# simplified call site (pseudo)
kernel.attend(kv_ptr, kv_stride, seq_len, n_heads)
# when pages fragmented we currently do:
temp = alloc(copy_size)
memcpy(temp, gather_paged(kv_pages))
kernel.attend(temp, ...)
```

sara: hmm. options: 1) pin pages and expose a contiguous scatter-gather mapping (needs DMA-friendly buffers), 2) implement a kernel scatter-gather read path so it can read non-contiguous pages directly (more invasive), 3) reduce copies by caching hot prefixes at runtime so most requests are contiguous.

nisha: also consider eviction interplay — pinning increases memory pressure and can amplify evictions, which then cause stalls. we could do an 'in-flight pin with lightweight refcount + deferred eviction' to avoid immediate writeback stalls.

kevin: do our device kernels accept anything like iovecs today? if so we might just adapt the ABI to pass a small vector of (page_ptr, len) entries and avoid the big copy.

jordan: unfortunately no — current kernels assume pointer+stride and contiguous layout. changing kernel ABI touches cuda/rocm/quantized backends and will need careful validation.

sara: short-term proposal: build a runtime adapter shim that composes a small contiguous buffer only for requested KV spans up to a threshold (e.g., 128KB). if the request exceeds threshold or number_of_fragments > N, route to a slower scatter-gather fallback kernel. add metrics: copy_bytes, pinned_pages, fallback_count.

nisha: agree. also add an eviction-safety test: simulate eviction during pin/unpin to ensure we don't get use-after-free.

kevin: long-term: invest in a true scatter-gather GPU kernel that reads a page indirection table (page_ids + offsets) so we can go zero-copy. that will remove memcopies but requires new low-level kernels and DMA validation.

jordan: plan: implement shim + short pins this sprint (1 week), add perf tests in nightly, then prototype SG kernel in Q2. i'll open an RFC + a perf dashboard. @sara @kevin can you help draft the kernel interface sketch? :thumbsup:

sara: ack. i'll add an architecture ticket and include sequence diagrams + expected telemetry. also adding canary: if fallback_rate > 5% for 10m we alert the team and flip to experimental SG kernel for impacted customers.

infra-bot: perf-run uploaded: /artifacts/paged-kv/1992345678/run-1 — baseline vs shim artifacts available.

kevin: nice. i'll add a stress eval focusing on long histories and variable page-fragmentation patterns.

jordan: thanks all — i'll post the implementation checklist and a small sequence diagram in the ticket. next steps: shim PR -> nightly perf -> eviction race tests -> SG kernel spike.
